reason: Start the sound-transmitting route by closing the ear canal with the eardrum.
expectation: I expect an outer ear with an eardrum positioned to vibrate in response to sound.

alternatives.reason: The membranes and hair cells also look like a useful starting point for the sensory path, but I prefer to follow sound from the outside inward.

effect: The eardrum now closes the ear canal, ready to connect to the middle ear.
reaction: The placement is straightforward and matches the expected route.
reason: Continue inward by connecting the eardrum to the ossicles.
expectation: I expect a connected chain that transmits eardrum vibrations toward the cochlea.

effect: The ossicles now connect the eardrum to the stapes, leaving the cochlear structures to build.
reaction: The explanation of how the small footplate drives the inner ear clarifies the connection.
reason: Fit the membranes into the cochlear chambers to build the next part of the sound route.
expectation: I expect a cochlear structure with its internal partition in place, ready to connect to the sensory cells.

alternatives.reason: The hair cells also need to join the membranes, but I want to establish their position in the cochlea first.

effect: The cochlear membranes are in place, but the sensory-cell layer is still missing.
reaction: The base-to-apex view helps locate the structures, though their different roles remain unclear.
reason: Add the hair cells to the cochlear membranes to complete the sensing surface.
expectation: I expect the hair cells to sit between the membranes, positioned for movement to bend their bundles.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hair cells to nerve fibres is also necessary, but I prefer to place them in the cochlea first.

effect: The sensory epithelium sits on the basilar membrane, with inner hair cells exposed for nerve connections.
reaction: The placement is clear, though how movement activates the cells remains to be explained.
reason: Connect the hair cells to the auditory nerve; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a cochlea whose sensory cells connect to nerve fibres leading toward the brain.

effect: The sensory cochlea now connects hair cells to auditory nerve fibres, distinguishing graded hair-cell signals from nerve action potentials.
reaction: The synapse explanation clarifies where the nerve spikes originate.
reason: Join the sound-transmitting ear to the sensory cochlea; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the stapes to connect to the cochlear oval window, allowing vibrations to reach its fluid and sensory structures.

effect: The stapes now meets the oval window, and the cochlear nerve is ready to connect to the body.
reaction: The free round window is a useful detail, though its role has not yet been explained.
reason: Connect the assembled ear to the body; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the ear and its auditory nerve to connect to brain pathways for hearing.
